text:
ana: heads up — ran spot procurement sim for next week's train runs, high eviction risk in us-west2 for A100s. thinking about mixing capacity-optimized pools with a small price-optimized overflow. thoughts?

matt: can you share numbers? eviction prob and cost delta?

ana: eviction ~18% over 12h window on us-west2 A100. price diff ~12% cheaper for price-opt pools but availability worse. When we tilt to capacity-opt we pay 9% more but evictions drop to 4%.

raj: 18% is rough. have we tried a tiered buffer: reserved warm buffer of on-demand + soft-preemptible pool with 60s drain TTL? that reduces coldstart pain.

ciara: we tried a 2% warm buffer for prod-rt in eu-west last month — cache miss rate dropped, latency stable. cost hit was acceptable. config was: 
```
pool_mix: {capacity_optimized: 0.7, price_optimized: 0.2, on_demand_buffer: 0.1}
eviction_ttl: 60
warmup_parallelism: 4
```

ana: nice, can we do region-aware mixes? maybe shift more capacity-opt to us-west and use price-opt in us-central as spill-over.

matt: yep. also consider proactive KV-state checkpointing. if a node is marked soon-to-preempt, replicate KV to warm buffer before eviction. avoids recompute.

raj: agree, but KV replication needs network budget. rank tradeoffs: KV_size vs expected recompute time. small KV -> replicate; large KV -> failover to cold restart.

ana: operationally, want a simple scoring function for pools: score = alpha*avail + beta*(1 - cost_norm) - gamma*latency_penalty. we can tune alpha/beta/gamma per SLA.

ciara: can we test via sim harness? run 1000 sims with variable alpha and measure p99 tail and cost. I'll take this.

capacity-bot: sim job queued: sim_2026_03_18_ana_pool_tuning (eta ~ 4h) :robot_face:

matt: also add fallback policy: if preemptions spike >10% for 10m, autoswap to on-demand buffer and increase capacity-opt weighting.

ana: ok assigning action items: ciara -> sims, raj -> KV replication heuristics doc, matt -> implement autoswap threshold + deploy runbook. I'll follow up with results.

ciara: on it. :thumbsup:
